events.title: Leibniz Uses Integral Calculus for the First Time
events.description: The German polymath Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz used integral calculus for the first time. He applied it to find the area under the graph of a function.
events.significance: This was a key step in the development of calculus. Leibniz's notation is still used in mathematics classrooms around the world.

events.title: Nat Turner Is Hanged in Virginia
events.description: Nat Turner was a enslaved preacher who led a violent slave uprising in Virginia. He was hanged in Jerusalem, Virginia, after it was put down.
events.significance: The rebellion hardened slaveholding attitudes in the South and led to harsher laws. It also became a powerful symbol of resistance to slavery.

events.title: Washington Becomes the 42nd U.S. State
events.description: Washington, named for the first U.S. president, was admitted to the Union as the 42nd state.
events.significance: Statehood helped open the Pacific Northwest to growth in timber, shipping and trade, and the state later became a major center of technology and industry.

events.title: Armistice Ends World War I
events.description: The Allies and Germany signed an armistice that ended the fighting of World War I on the Western Front.
events.significance: The day is remembered every year as Armistice Day or Remembrance Day, and in the United States as Veterans Day.

events.title: Angola Declares Independence
events.description: Angola gained independence from Portugal and became a sovereign nation after centuries of colonial rule.
events.significance: Independence marked the end of Portugal's African empire in Angola, though the country then fell into a long civil war.
